newsitem.title: INDIA: India rulers face test vote amid talk of snap poll.
newsitem.headline: India rulers face test vote amid talk of snap poll.

text.p: India's embattled coalition prepared to face a vote of confidence in parliament on Friday after talks to end a political crisis were deadlocked.
Prospects of a snap poll loomed large. Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's alliance said it was ready to face elections.

The centre-left United Front remained defiant against its former ally the Congress party, which withdrew its support on March 30, threatening the 10-month-old government formed after inconclusive general elections.
Patch-up talks broke down on Thursday after the 15-party alliance of free-marketers, regional groups and communists rejected a Congress demand that it replace Deve Gowda as its leader.

Both groups hoped for a political miracle before a 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) deadline set by Congress for Deve Gowda to step down or face a hostile vote. Congress has already issued a whip asking its party lawmakers to be present.
Parliament was scheduled to convene at the time of the deadline and debate on a confidence motion before voting on the government later on Friday.
"Our stand is final. There is no question of a change of leadership," United Front leader Harkishen Singh Surjeet said.
Congress president Sitaram Kesri had asked for Deve Gowda's ouster, saying he was not containing "communal forces," a reference to the Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Analysts have said Congress was banking on divisions within the United Front to provide new allies it could lead. But the United Front has so far spoken in one voice.

Last year Congress and the 15-party alliance made common cause to oust a 12-day-old government formed by the BJP, which emerged as the single largest group in the 545-seat Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament.

The Congress has 140 members. The United Front, which has 178 members and a dozen other backers, can survive only if the BJP abstains instead of voting out the government. The BJP and its allies control 193 votes in parliament.

If the government falls, President Shankar Dayal Sharma can choose to invite the BJP once again to form a new government, or seek out another group which he believes can form a new government. The Congress is a prospective candidate.
Most parties are dreading a third prospect, that of a snap election. Delhi's political pundits say this could lead to new combinations in the fragmented parliament.
Congress has said it is willing to negotiate a new political arrangement (with the United Front) to contain the BJP, even if the coalition falls as a result of its own vote.
The Hindu nationalist BJP is eyeing a snap poll in which it sees good chances for itself, but has said it does not want Congress to lead a caretaker government if snap polls are held.
The party has decided to finalise its stand only on Friday.
The United Front said it was prepared to face the electorate if Deve Gowda was defeated in parliament. "It is reasonable to expect elections in May or June," a senior alliance official said.

Political uncertainty cast its shadow on the stock market, and also on Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's market-friendly budget presented on February 28., which proposed tax cuts that parliament is yet to approve.
